definition.description: Start seated in a compact tuck on a clean stable mat or floor, holding the shins. Rock backward only to controlled upper-back and shoulder contact, rock forward, place both feet under the body, and stand tall without placing hands on the floor or another person. One seated-tuck to tall-standing return is one cycle. Hand or partner assistance, raised surfaces, repeated rocks returning to seated, forward or backward rolls, changed terminal positions, assessment, and clinical intervention require separate reviewed variants or definitions.

environment.space: one roll-to-stand station with a clear lateral boundary and exit
inspection: clear roll path and stand exit
environment.changeRule: Changing start, contact path, hand or partner assistance, surface height or incline, terminal position, load, intent, symptoms, or substitution requires revalidation.

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 81 is reauthored as one exact no-hand seated-tuck rock-to-tall cycle; assistance and other rolling paths remain separate.

anatomy.claimsBoundary: Observable task mechanics and likely loading sites only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, isolated activation, or guaranteed-transfer claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Practises a compact tuck rock and controlled no-hand return to standing.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Hold your shins, rock only to your upper back and shoulders, bring both feet under you, then stand tall without hands.
secondaryCues: keep the tuck compact and breathe
keep pressure off the head and neck
make the rock smaller before using your hands
pause and reset after every tall finish
unexpectedSensations: dizziness, chest symptoms, unusual breathlessness, numbness, tingling, weakness, or loss of control
selfChecks: upper back and shoulders—not head or neck—take the rock contact
no hand, partner, or surface assistance
both feet come under the body before standing
finish tall and balanced with no stop symptom

observationChecklist: exact seated tuck, upper-back/shoulder rock, and no-hand tall return
surface, clearance, communication, head/neck clearance, hands, feet, balance, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.head_or_neck_contact: stop and reduce or change task; do not continue through head or neck pressure
faultCorrections.hand_use: reset; hand assistance is a different reviewed variant
faultCorrections.uncontrolled_stand: reduce cycle count and restore a stable feet-under-body return before continuing

station, floor access, communication, or symptoms conflict with exact task

snapshot.description: Athlete begins seated in a tuck. They rock back onto the upper back/shoulders, then rock forward and attempt to place feet under the body to stand tall.

variants.displayName: Seated Tuck Rock-to-Tall Stand — Stable Floor, No-Hand

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate no-hand tuck-rock-to-tall practice when exact floor, contact, and budget conditions fit.

dosage.countRule: count only a seated compact tuck, controlled upper-back/shoulder rock, forward return, both feet under body, tall no-hand stand, and deliberate reset

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The tuck stays compact; contact stays at the upper back/shoulders with head and neck clear; no hand or partner support is used; both feet come under the body; standing balance, breathing, and symptoms remain acceptable.
stopRules: stop on pain, head/neck contact or pressure, new symptoms, unsafe station, uncontrolled stand, repeated hand use, or participant request
stop when smaller rock, fewer cycles, and longer rest cannot restore the exact cycle
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Check floor, clear exit, stop signal, and exact no-hand boundary; demonstrate a small controlled rock; observe contact, hands, feet, balance, symptoms, and first quality loss; count only valid cycles.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Hold your shins, rock to your upper back and shoulders, bring both feet under you, stand tall without hands, then reset.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate compact-rock and floor-to-stand practice only; no guaranteed transfer is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: smaller rock, fewer cycles, longer rest, or another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add hand or partner assistance, surface height/incline, load, repeated rocks, or a different roll direction without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Tuck tight, upper back only, feet under, stand tall without hands.
supportPrompts.coach: A repeated seated rock or assisted stand is not this exact card.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact floor, no-hand contact path, controlled stand, symptoms, communication, dose, and current budgets—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: confirm stable surface, exit, communication, and stop signal
confirm upper-back/shoulder contact with head/neck clear
confirm a controlled no-hand feet-under-body stand
stopSigns: sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, or post-trauma pain or stop request
head/neck contact or pressure, dizziness, chest symptoms, unusual breathlessness, neurologic or circulation concern
unsafe surface, repeated hand use, uncontrolled contact, or uncontrolled stand
contraindications: symptom, restriction, or unsafe setting conflict with exact floor rolling
assisted, raised, inclined, repeated rocking, forward/backward-roll, assessment, or clinical intent
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after requirements, duration, and fatigue budgets are recomputed.
Do not treat assisted stands, tuck rocks, forward/backward rolls, or raised-surface work as automatic substitutions.
